cards.title: A homeowner pays the balance by card
cards.whyManualNote: The card form is NMI's own secure form. The everyday automated tests use a stand-in, and the one test that loads the real form runs on a developer's computer, never on the test site.
cards.precondition: The test accounts were reset after anyone last paid as Jordan Pryce, so his balance is $250.00. If the balance is not $250.00, or the page says "Online payments not yet available", record Blocked. If the card fields never appear inside the payment window, the payment sandbox is down: record Blocked, not Fail. If the window reads "Payment not processed" after you press "Pay $250.00", someone may have paid the same amount with the same test card in the last 20 minutes, which the payment sandbox refuses: wait 20 minutes, press "Try again", and record Blocked if it happens a second time.

steps.do: Sign in as Jordan Pryce and choose "Payments" in the menu (on a phone, tap "More" first).
steps.see: Under "Outstanding Balance" it reads $250.00, marked "Payment due".

steps.do: Press "Make a Payment" at the top of the page.
steps.see: A window titled "Make a payment" opens with "Pay full balance ($250.00)" selected and 250.00 in "Amount to pay".

steps.do: Press "Continue · $250.00" and check that "Card" is chosen under "Pay with".
steps.see: "Total" reads $250.00, and a card form appears inside the window with fields for the card number, the expiration date and the security code.

steps.do: Enter the sandbox test card from the account panel (and its ZIP code if the form asks), leave "Save this card for AutoPay" unticked, and press "Pay $250.00".
steps.see: The window reads "Payment received", with "Amount paid" $250.00, a "Confirmation" number, "Date" showing today's date and time, and "Remaining due" $0.00.

steps.do: Press "Done".
steps.see: "Outstanding Balance" reads $0.00, marked "All clear". On the tab "Account history", the top row of "Payment History" shows today's date, $250.00, "Payment received" and the same confirmation number.

lookFor: Did the card form look like part of HOAhx, not a different website?
Was it clear, before you confirmed, exactly how much you were paying?
Was the amount you owe easy to find as soon as the page opened?
cards.reset: The payment stays, and Jordan Pryce's balance reads $0.00, until the next reset of the test accounts. The card "Two board members void a homeowner's card payment, on two phones" uses this payment and cancels it.

steps.see: The window closes. Under "Approvals waiting for you", in "Waiting for someone else (1)", the row "Void $250.00 to Jordan Pryce" reads "Waiting for approval" and "Requested by you", with the time left to decide.

cards.title: A home seller pays the community's transfer package fee with the real card form, and the president sees the receipt
cards.whyManualNote: The fee is a real charge through the payment processor's sandbox (NMI), typed into its own card fields; the automated tests use a made-up payment reply. If the processor's sandbox is down, record Blocked, not Fail.
cards.precondition: The person who looks after the test site has set Cedar Hollow's transfer package fee to $1.00 (the sandbox declines anything under $1.00) and has switched Cedar Hollow's payments on. Use this card in place of the package step of the check "An owner reports the sale of a home and asks for the transfer package, and the president marks it ready", never after it: if Mei Tanaka already asked for the package, record Blocked until the test accounts are reset. Use two browsers or a private window. If the payment form never appears, record Blocked.

steps.do: As the seller: sign in as Mei Tanaka, choose "My Home" and open the tab "Ownership transfer". If no sale is open, set "Expected closing date" to today, type your own name in "Buyer's name" and your own e-mail address in "Buyer's e-mail", then press "Report a sale".
steps.see: The heading "Selling your home" shows "Buyer:" with your name and the status "Sale reported".

steps.do: As the seller: read the box "Transfer package".
steps.see: It says "Your community charges $1.00 for the transfer package." and has a button "Pay $1.00 and ask for the transfer package". There is no button "Ask for the transfer package".

steps.do: As the seller: press "Pay $1.00 and ask for the transfer package".
steps.see: It says "Pay $1.00 for the transfer package. No card fee is added." and shows the choices "Card" and "Bank account" with the payment provider's card fields.

steps.do: As the seller: press "Pay $1.00" with the fields empty.
steps.see: A red message reads "Enter your card or bank account details to pay the fee." Nothing is charged.

steps.do: As the seller: with "Card" chosen, enter the sandbox test card (it is on the account panel) and press "Pay $1.00".
steps.see: A message reads "Fee paid and transfer package requested. The board will tell you when it is ready." The box now says "Transfer package requested" and "Transfer package fee paid", with "$1.00 on" today's date and a receipt number.

steps.do: As the president: sign in as Dana Whitfield (password, then the two-step code), choose "Properties" and click the row for 31 Birch Court.
steps.see: The panel shows "Transfer package requested", "The community charges $1.00 for the package. The seller pays it when asking." and "Transfer package fee paid" with $1.00 and the same receipt number the seller saw.

lookFor: Did the seller know before paying what the $1.00 was for and that nothing is saved?
Was the receipt clear enough to keep as proof of payment?
cards.expectNotProvable: A bank payment for this fee coming back unpaid cannot be produced on the sandbox, and the page does not handle that case yet.
cards.reset: The sale of 31 Birch Court stays reported with the package requested and the $1.00 receipt until the next reset of the test accounts puts the cast back.

cards.title: A title company gets the e-mail for a home's transfer package, signs in from its link and opens the package
cards.whyManualNote: The link reaches the title company as a real e-mail through HOA HX's e-mail service, and the link in that e-mail must open the package after sign-in; the automated tests never see an inbox and open the link by its address. If the e-mail service is down and no e-mail comes, record Blocked, not Fail.
cards.precondition: Run this after the check "An owner reports the sale of a home and asks for the transfer package, and the president marks it ready" (with the note "Ready to collect at the office") and before the check where the president names the buyer and confirms the handoff: 31 Birch Court needs a reported sale with its package marked ready. You play the title company with your own e-mail address that you can read now and that already has an account on the test site with a confirmed address (the test accounts' addresses receive nothing). Use two browsers or a private window for the title company. If 31 Birch Court has no reported sale, record Blocked.

steps.do: As the president: sign in as Dana Whitfield (password, then the two-step code), choose "Properties" in the menu and open 31 Birch Court.
steps.see: The panel shows "A sale is reported for this home" with "Expected closing" and a date (write that date down) and "Prepared on" and a date (write that date down), and a box "Title company access" that reads "No title company can open this package." with a button "Share with a title company".

steps.do: As the president: press "Share with a title company".
steps.see: A form opens with the fields "Title company's e-mail", "Company name", "Last day they can open it" and "Reason", and the buttons "Not now" and "Share the package".

steps.do: As the president: type your own e-mail address in "Title company's e-mail", "Summit Title" in "Company name", a day one week from today in "Last day they can open it" and "The title company asked for the closing papers" in "Reason", then press "Share the package". If a box titled "Confirm it is you" opens, enter Dana Whitfield's password and press "Continue". If a second box titled "Confirm it’s you" then asks for a six-digit code, enter the two-step code from the account panel and press "Confirm". The share then goes through by itself.
steps.see: (The message stays on screen only a few seconds, so look for it right after you press the button.) A message reads "The title company can now open the package. We e-mailed them the link." The box shows "Summit Title" with your address, "Can open this sale's package through" the day you chose, and "shared by Dana Whitfield".

steps.do: As the title company: open your inbox for that address (look in spam too).
steps.see: One e-mail has arrived in your inbox, not in spam, with the subject "Transfer package for 31 Birch Court". It says who shared the transfer package for the home in Cedar Hollow with you for its closing, that nobody else can open the link, and the last day you can open it (the day you chose, written out with the month name). It has a button "Open the transfer package". It names no seller, buyer or amount.

steps.do: As the title company: in a browser where nobody is signed in to the test site, press "Open the transfer package" in the e-mail.
steps.see: The test site's log in page opens and asks for your "Email address".

steps.do: As the title company: type your address, press "Continue", enter your password and press "Log in". If asked for a text or authenticator code, enter the one for your own account.
steps.see: You land on the transfer package itself, not on a home screen or a menu. The page shows "Cedar Hollow", the address of 31 Birch Court, "Expected closing" with the same closing date you wrote down in step 1, and "Transfer package ready".

steps.do: As the title company: read the rest of the page.
steps.see: It says "Prepared on" with the date you wrote down in step 1 and the note "Ready to collect at the office" (typed in the earlier check). Between that and the access lines, the page shows a box headed "Before closing" with a "Balance:" line for the home (31 Birch Court owes nothing, so it reads "Nothing due"), followed by either "Nothing is due and nothing is open on this home." or the list of open items. It does not read "We couldn't load the account review. Try again in a moment." Near the end it says "You can open this package through" the last day the president chose, "Shared by Dana Whitfield", "Access also ends when the sale is handed over or cancelled" and "Signed in as" with your address.

lookFor: Was it clear from the e-mail alone who sent the package and what to do with it?
Did the e-mail look like it came from HOA HX, and was its sender what you would expect?
Did the package page show only the home, the closing date, the package status and the "Before closing" box, with nothing about the seller's private notes?
cards.reset: Your address keeps access to the package until its last day, the handoff of the sale, or a cancellation. To clear it sooner, the president opens 31 Birch Court, presses "End access", gives a reason and presses "End access" again. The next reset of the test accounts clears it too.

Does the line under the two buttons ("We still send the code to that address, and your community is added to that account.") match what happened?

cards.title: A homeowner resets a forgotten password from the e-mail HOA HX sends
cards.whyManualNote: The reset link is a real e-mail sent by HOA HX's e-mail service, and its one-time code is made by the sign-in service; the automated tests never see an inbox and make the code themselves. If the e-mail service is down and no e-mail comes, record Blocked, not Fail.
cards.precondition: Use an account on the test site made with your own e-mail address that you can read now (for example an account you made earlier on the test site with your own address), with a confirmed address and no two-step sign-in. Do not use a test account: its address receives nothing, and a new password would lock everyone else out of it. You start signed out. The password of your account changes in this check.

steps.do: Go to the test site's address followed by /auth/forgot-password.
steps.see: The page "Reset your password" says "Enter your email and we'll send you a link to reset your password." It has the field "Email address" and the button "Send reset link".

steps.do: Type your own address in "Email address" and press "Send reset link".
steps.see: The page "Check your email" says "If an account exists for" your address "we sent a password reset link." It offers "Resend reset link" and "Back to sign in".

steps.do: Open your inbox (look in spam too).
steps.see: One e-mail has arrived in your inbox, not in spam, with the subject "Reset your HOA HX password". It says "Someone asked to reset the password of your HOA HX account.", has a button "Choose a new password", and says the link works once, for one hour, and the new password needs at least 15 characters.

steps.do: Press "Choose a new password" in the e-mail.
steps.see: The test site opens (its address, not another site's) on a page "Set new password" with the fields "New Password" and "Confirm Password" and the button "Set New Password".

steps.do: Type a password of 8 characters in both fields.
steps.see: The button "Set New Password" cannot be pressed, and a note under "New Password" lists what the password still needs (the field's hint reads "At least 15 characters").

steps.do: Replace both with a new password of at least 15 characters that you will remember, then press "Set New Password".
steps.see: The page "Password Updated" says "Your password has been successfully changed. You can now sign in with your new password." and offers the button "Log in now".

steps.do: Press "Log in now", then type your address in "Email address" and tap "Continue", and type the new password in "Password" and press "Log in".
steps.see: The sign-in form is gone and the page shows the homeowner's menu with Payments in it.

steps.do: Press "Choose a new password" in the same e-mail a second time.
steps.see: The page "Link Expired" says "This password reset link has expired or is invalid. Reset links are only valid for 1 hour." and offers "Request a New Link".

lookFor: Did the e-mail look like it came from HOA HX, and was its sender what you would expect?
Was it clear from the e-mail alone what to do and how long you had?
Did the page tell you plainly what a good new password needs?
cards.reset: Your account keeps the new password. The reset of the test accounts does not touch it.

cards.title: A homeowner's installed iPhone app shows a changed screen after a phone update, with no store update
cards.whyManualNote: The app downloads, checks and switches to its new screens by itself on a real iPhone, on its next launch; no browser test can install the app, close it and open it again. If the update job did not run or is red, or the build on the phone is too old to take the update, record Blocked, not Fail.
cards.precondition: The latest HOA HX test build from TestFlight is on the iPhone and has not been opened since the change was published to the test site's phone updates. The person who looks after the test site has checked that the job "Publish phone live update (staging)" for that change is green, and has told you one screen and one word or line on it that is different in the new version (the "marked line"), and the name of the version before it. If the marked line already shows on the phone before step 2, record Blocked and ask for a reset of the phone: delete the app and install it again from TestFlight.

steps.do: Open the HOA HX app on the iPhone and sign in as Jordan Pryce: type his email (from the account panel) in "Email address" and tap "Continue", then type the password in "Password" and tap "Log in".
steps.see: The homeowner's home page opens with Jordan Pryce's name on it and no blank white page.

steps.do: Go to the screen named in the run notes and find the marked line.
steps.see: The screen shows the old wording, not the marked line.

steps.do: Stay on that screen for one minute and use it as usual.
steps.see: The screen does not reload or change by itself while you use it.

steps.do: Close the app completely (swipe up from the bottom and flick the app away), then open it again.
steps.see: The app opens within about 12 seconds on the home page, still signed in as Jordan Pryce, with no blank white page.

steps.do: Go to the screen Jacob named again.
steps.see: The marked line now shows. The rest of the screen is as before.

steps.do: Close the app completely and open it once more.
steps.see: The marked line still shows and the app does not ask for the password.

lookFor: Did the app ever show a blank white page or an error while it changed over?
Was there any sign to a homeowner that the screens had changed, and did it need any action from them?
cards.reset: The phone stays on the new version. The check "A homeowner's installed iPhone app goes back to its earlier screens when the update is rolled back" goes next. Deleting the app and installing it again from TestFlight puts it back on the screens built into it.

cards.title: A homeowner's installed iPhone app goes back to its earlier screens when the update is rolled back
cards.whyManualNote: The rollback is started by hand on the project's Actions page, and only a real iPhone, closed and opened again, shows whether the app takes the earlier screens back without a store update. If the rollback run is red, or the phone was not on the new version at the start, record Blocked, not Fail.
cards.precondition: Run this straight after the check "A homeowner's installed iPhone app shows a changed screen after a phone update, with no store update", so the phone is on the new version and shows the marked line written in the run notes. The person who looks after the test site has the id of the earlier version (a code like 20261021.812-ab12cd3, from the earlier card's note) and can start the "Live update control" run on the project's Actions page.

steps.do: On the iPhone open the HOA HX app (signed in as Jordan Pryce) and go to the screen with the marked line.
steps.see: The marked line shows (the new version).

steps.do: As the person who looks after the test site (on a computer, not the phone): on the project's Actions page choose "Live update control", press "Run workflow", set "Which phones" to staging, "action" to rollback, type the earlier version's id in "bundle_id", and run it.
steps.see: The run finishes green.

steps.do: On the iPhone close the app completely and open it again.
steps.see: The app opens on the home page, still signed in as Jordan Pryce, with no blank white page. The marked line may still show: the earlier screens are taken on the launch after this one.

steps.do: Close the app completely and open it once more, then go to the screen with the marked line.
steps.see: The app opens within about 12 seconds with no blank white page, and the marked line is gone: the earlier wording is back.

steps.do: Choose "Payments" in the menu (tap "More" first).
steps.see: The page opens with "Outstanding Balance", and you are still signed in as Jordan Pryce.

lookFor: Did the app ever show a blank white page or an error while it changed back?
Was everything else on the screens you opened the same as before the rollback?
cards.reset: The phone stays on the earlier version. Deleting the app and installing it again from TestFlight puts it back on the screens built into it. The next push to the test site publishes a new version.

cards.title: The president asks for a copy of the community's records on the live site and the download starts
cards.whyManualNote: The download link must be made by the live site's own download service, and the page hands out no other kind of link (it says the file cannot be opened right now); the test machines swap in a plain link, and the test site's permissions are not the live site's.
cards.precondition: Jacob approves this run and does it himself, on the live site, signed in as the President (or Account Owner) of a community that holds only test data. If only a real community exists, record Blocked: its file would hold real residents. Nobody else runs it. The file holds only the lists that person's role may export. The sign-in is the live test community's own President (or Account Owner), held by Jacob; it is not the test-site account.

steps.do: Sign in as the President (password, then the two-step code) and open the live site's page "My Subscription" (menu "Financial", "My Subscription").
steps.see: The page "HOA Platform Subscription" opens and, near the bottom, a box "A copy of the community's records" says it is one ZIP file with the residents, the board, maintenance requests and violations, cleaned of private details.

steps.do: Press "Ask for a copy" (or "Ask for a new copy" if one is listed).
steps.see: A box asks "Why do you need the copy?" and offers "Prepare the file" and "Not now".

steps.do: Type "Checking that the download works on the live site" and press "Prepare the file". If a box titled "Confirm it is you" opens, enter the password and press "Continue"; if a second box titled "Confirm it’s you" asks for a six-digit code, enter it and press "Confirm".
steps.see: The page reads "The file is being prepared. Keep this page open; it takes a minute or two." and then shows a file name beginning "community-records-" and ending ".zip", its size, the day it was prepared, and "You can download it until" a date 7 days away, with one line for each list and its number of rows.

steps.do: Press "Download the file". If "Confirm it is you" opens again, confirm as before.
steps.see: A ZIP file starts downloading to the computer and the page stays where it is. The page does not say "The file cannot be opened right now. Try again in a few minutes." and does not say "The download could not start. Try again." Under the button it says the link works for 15 minutes.

steps.do: Open the downloaded ZIP file on the computer.
steps.see: It holds one spreadsheet (CSV) file for each list named on the page. No file has a column for an e-mail address, a phone number or a birth date.

lookFor: Was it clear on the page how long the file and the download link last?
Did the page say anything about who asked for the file and why (the billing log)?
cards.reset: The file stays on the live site for 7 days and is then removed; the request and the download are in the billing log with the reason. Delete the downloaded ZIP from the computer. Nothing a homeowner can see is changed.

cards.title: A homeowner signs in with a passkey in the iPhone app

steps.do: Approve the phone's sheet with Face ID or the passcode.

cards.title: A homeowner signs in with a passkey in the Android app
cards.whyManualNote: The passkey is made and used by the Android phone itself (its own passkey sheet and screen lock); a desktop browser in a test has neither.
cards.precondition: The test accounts were reset today. The HOA HX app from the latest test build is installed on the Android phone, and the phone has a screen lock (a fingerprint, face unlock or a PIN) and is signed in to a Google account. HOAhx staff have switched passkeys on for the test site: if "Log in with a passkey" never appears on the sign-in page, record Blocked, not Fail. If the test site itself is down, record Blocked. A "Confirm it’s you" panel may appear before adding or removing a passkey; if it does, follow it.

steps.do: Open the HOA HX app on the Android phone. Sign in as Mei Tanaka: type her email (from the account panel) in "Email address" and tap "Continue", then type her password in "Password" and tap "Log in".
steps.see: Mei Tanaka's dashboard opens. (If the page asks for a code, type the one from the account panel.)

steps.do: Tap "Account" in the bar at the bottom of the screen.
steps.see: The page headed "My Account" opens.

steps.do: Scroll down to the card headed "Privacy & Security" and find the block named "Passkeys". Tap "Add a passkey".
steps.see: A panel headed "Add a passkey" opens with a field "Passkey name". It says the device will ask for Face ID, a fingerprint or its PIN.

steps.do: Type "My Android phone" in "Passkey name" and tap "Add passkey".
steps.see: The phone shows its own sheet asking you to save a passkey for HOA HX. If a "Confirm it’s you" panel comes first, type the password in "Password" and tap "Continue".

steps.do: Approve the phone's sheet with the fingerprint, face unlock or the screen PIN.
steps.see: The panel closes. Under "Your passkeys" a line reads "My Android phone" with "Added" and today's date, "not used yet", and the buttons "Rename" and "Remove". No red message is shown.

steps.do: Tap "More" in the bar at the bottom, then tap "Log out" at the foot of the menu, then tap "Yes, log out".
steps.see: The sign-in page opens.

steps.do: On the first step of the sign-in page, without typing anything, tap "Log in with a passkey".
steps.see: The button reads "Waiting for your passkey…" and the phone shows its own sheet offering the passkey you saved. The page does not say "This phone has no passkey for HOA HX yet" or "Passkey sign-in did not work".

steps.do: Approve the phone's sheet with the fingerprint, face unlock or the screen PIN.
steps.see: Mei Tanaka's dashboard opens without the password being asked for.

steps.do: Tap "Account", scroll to "Passkeys" under "Privacy & Security".
steps.see: "My Android phone" now reads "last used" with today's date, not "not used yet".

steps.do: On the line "My Android phone", tap "Remove". A panel headed "Remove My Android phone?" opens; tap "Remove passkey".
steps.see: If a "Confirm it’s you" panel appears, type the password in "Password" and tap "Continue". Then the line "My Android phone" is gone from "Your passkeys".

lookFor: Did the phone's own passkey sheet appear straight away, with no delay that left you unsure whether anything was happening?
Did every message on the screen read in plain words a homeowner could follow?
cards.reset: The passkey is removed in the last step. If the check stopped sooner, tap "Remove" on the line "My Android phone" under "Passkeys" on the "My Account" page, then "Remove passkey"; the next reset of the test accounts also clears it. The passkey on the phone itself is harmless once HOA HX no longer knows it.
